record.original_question: For a graph Γ on n vertices, must its Seidel energy satisfy S(Γ) >= 2(n - 1), with equality at the complete graph K_n?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.35. If Γ is a graph on n vertices, then S(Γ) ≥ S(Kn) = 2(n − 1).
Ghorbani [38] proved the Haemers’ conjecture in the case det(S) ≥ n − 1 and very recently, Akbari, Einollahzadeh, Karkhaneei and Nematollah [2] finished the proof of the conjecture.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Γ be a simple graph on n vertices. The Seidel matrix S(Γ) of Γ is the n×n symmetric matrix with diagonal entries 0, off-diagonal entry −1 in position (i,j) if vertices i and j are adjacent, and +1 otherwise. The Seidel energy of Γ is defined as
   S(Γ) = ∑_{i=1}^n |λ_i|,
where λ_1,…,λ_n are the eigenvalues of S(Γ).

Prove or disprove: for every graph Γ on n vertices,
   S(Γ) ≥ 2(n − 1),
with equality attained at the complete graph K_n.
artifact.status_search_result: Haemers' conjecture on the Seidel energy of graphs has been proved. Ghorbani established the inequality under the additional assumption |det S(Γ)| ≥ n−1, and the general case was settled by Akbari, Einollahzadeh, Karkhaneei and Nematollahi (arXiv:1901.06692, published in European Journal of Combinatorics, 2020). A short proof was later given (Linear Algebra and its Applications, 2024).

status_evidence.title: Proof of a Conjecture on the Seidel Energy of Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Haemers conjectured that the Seidel energy of any graph of order n is at least 2n-2... We establish the validity of Haemers' Conjecture in general.
status_evidence.claim: Haemers' Seidel energy conjecture is proved for all n.

status_evidence.title: A short proof of Haemers' conjecture on the Seidel energy of graphs
status_evidence.snippet: A short proof of Haemers' conjecture on the Seidel energy of graphs.
status_evidence.claim: A subsequent short proof confirms the conjecture is settled.
